newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Legal battle over historic Manila Hotel intensifies.
newsitem.headline: Legal battle over historic Manila Hotel intensifies.

text.p: A legal battle over the historic Manila Hotel intensified on Wednesday after a Philippine state agency which owns the hotel said the Supreme Court could not force it into selling the property to a local company.

The Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) told the Supreme Court that a recent court order had violated their rights as hotel owners by depriving them of a chance to get the best possible deal for the 75-year-old hotel.
On February 3, the Supreme Court, voided a successful bid by Malaysian infrastructure firm Renong Berhad for the hotel following a public tender.
The court's decision followed a petition by the losing bidder -- Manila Prince Hotel Corporation, which had later offered to match the Malaysian firm's bid.
The court, citing a "Filipino First" policy, upheld Manila Prince's contention that the Manila Hotel was part of the country's heritage and should not be sold to a foreign group.

In a petition seeking the Supreme Court to reconsider its ruling, government counsel Oscar Garcia said the GSIS could not implement the court's order to sell Manila Hotel to Manila Prince Corporation because there was no such sale agreement.

"To coerce respondent GSIS to simply execute the necesary contract pursuant to the bidding guidelines is tantamount to stripping respondent GSIS of its right to negotiate for reasonable terms and conditions in the operation of the hotel," the petition said.
The Supreme Court did not say when it would rule on the GSIS appeal.
